description: A learner stuck mid-task on what the lesson assumes is offered a detour for it, takes it, and comes back to the task they were doing, with their destination untouched.

profile.background: Fifteen years of Java and some Go. New to Python: I can read it, but I have never used dataclasses, decorators, or any of that.
profile.why: Joining the billing team; need to be useful in Python.

then: I keep getting stuck on the Line thing. Where is its constructor? I searched for __init__ and there isn't one, so I don't understand how these objects are being built, and I can't tell what I'm supposed to change.
yes, that would help, let's do that first

graders.name: offers a detour, with its steps, and says the task waits
graders.criteria: At the point where the learner says they are stuck on how Line objects are built, the tutor recognises this as a gap in general Python knowledge (dataclasses) rather than a question about the invoice rule, and offers a short detour for it: it names what the detour would cover, as one to three steps, and makes clear the learner's current task is waiting for them and will come back. The offer is an offer: it stops for the learner's answer rather than starting the detour in the same turn. Answering the immediate question about dataclasses as well is fine, and good; what fails is never offering the detour, or taking it without asking.

graders.name: takes it on the yes and comes back to the task
graders.criteria: After the learner agrees, the tutor takes the detour and serves its first step as a lesson, grounded in this repository's own files rather than as a generic tutorial. When the learner then says they are done, the tutor moves the detour along without being asked: either to a next step, or, if that was the only step, back to the invoice-totals task, saying which they are now in. At the end the learner is told where they are in plain terms. It never tells them to run any plumbing themselves, and it never says the lesson they were doing is finished or satisfied.
